news.headline: Astronauts Get Ready for Spacewalk No. 100
news.body: This Thursday, two astronauts will float outside the International Space Station to give it more power. Anil Menon from NASA and Joshua Kutryk from Canada will add a new solar panel that rolls out like a giant mat to soak up sunlight. NASA is calling it U.S. spacewalk number 100! A second spacewalk on November 5 will add one more panel, the last of eight new roll-out panels. Together, they can boost the station's power by up to 30 percent.

news.headline: Two Rare Leopard Cubs Are Born in Europe
news.body: Two Sri Lankan leopard cubs were born at Ostrava Zoo in the country of Czechia, about an hour apart. Their mom is an experienced mother, and she is taking care of the cubs all by herself while keepers give the family peace and quiet. These leopards are rare, with fewer than 60 living in 27 zoos that are part of a European breeding program. The cubs are the only ones born in that program in the past year! Their first checkup with the vet will happen when they are a month old.

news.headline: The World's Biggest Serving of French Fries!
news.body: Potato lovers in Boise, Idaho, just set a delicious world record. Volunteers from a restaurant called Spud Daddy and the Idaho Potato Commission cooked a giant pile of French fries in four huge fryers. It weighed 1,474 pounds, about as heavy as a full-grown cow! That beat the old record, which had stood since 2018. When the weighing was done, the crowd got to munch on the record-breaking fries.

fun_fact: Leopards are amazing climbers. They often nap up in trees, and they're strong enough to carry their dinner way up into the branches! 🌳

this_day_in_history: On October 26, 1825, the Erie Canal opened in New York. This 363-mile waterway let boats travel all the way from the Great Lakes to New York City! 🚤
did_you_know: Potatoes were the first vegetable ever grown in space! Potato plants grew aboard the space shuttle Columbia in 1995. 🚀
